figures.finding: The Children's Law 2011 defines a child as anyone under eighteen and, by its amending Act, substitutes 'eighteen' for 'twenty-one' wherever it appears in the Domestic Relations Law and 'child' for 'minor', so the age at which the domestic-relations law ends minority is eighteen. No single civil-code article stating 'majority' was read.

value.basis: Children's Law 2011, Act amending the Domestic Relations Law (Title 9), s. 1(a)-(b); s. 2 child under 18

sources.said: “Child” shall mean any person below the age of 18 years; … Section 1. The Domestic Relations Law is amended as follows: (a) by substituting the words “twenty-one” with the word “eighteen” wherever the word “twenty-one” appears; (b) by substituting the word “minor” with the word “child.”

figures.finding: No child under fifteen may be employed full time; from thirteen a child may do light work for at most two hours a day and fourteen a week; under sixteen, at most seven hours a day and forty-two a week with an hour's rest and no more than four hours at a stretch. The Minister may make regulations for a permit letting an employer engage a child under thirteen for artistic performances, and for times of day; no such regulations were found, so under thirteen a child performer has no lawful route until they exist. Work for long hours or at night is hazardous work barred to all children. Nothing distinguishes writing or directing.

value.under13ArtisticPermit: by regulation of the Minister (s. 21.7(b)); regulations not found

figures.applies: Liberia (Decent Work Act 2015, Part on child labour, §§ 21.2 to 21.7).

sources.said: No person shall employ, or allow a child under the age of 15 years to be employed in full time employment. … a) A child who is at least 13 years old may be employed to perform light work, provided that they: i) may only work for a maximum of two hours in a day and fourteen hours in a week; … a) A child who has not yet attained the age of 16 years may not be employed for more than 7 hours in any day, or for more than 42 hours in any working week. b) Daily hours of work for children shall include one or more rest periods totaling at least one hour, with rest periods so arranged that a child does not work for more than four consecutive hours.

The Minister may make regulations: a) Establishing a system by which an employer shall obtain a permit from the Ministry to engage a child to perform light work; b) Establishing a system by which an employer might obtain a permit to engage a child younger than 13 for such purposes as participation in artistic performances; c) Stipulating times of day during which children may work or shall not work, as the case may be;
v) work under particularly difficult conditions such as work for long hours or during the night, or work where the child is unreasonably confined to the premises of the employer.

figures.finding: A child's contract of employment or apprenticeship is lawful only with the parent's or guardian's consent and under a licence from the Ministry of Labor; no rule setting a child's earnings aside was found.

value.binding: parent's or guardian's consent and a Ministry of Labor licence (Children's Law s. 9.3)

sources.said: Any contract for apprenticeship or employment shall be with the consent of the child’s parent or guardian, consistent with the provisions of subsections 1 and 2 of this section and all other applicable laws and regulations, and under license from the Ministry of Labor.
